items.stem: The axial normal stress in a bar of cross-sectional area A carrying axial force F is:

options.rationale: Correct: normal stress sigma = F/A for uniform axial loading.
Multiplying force by area does not give stress; units would be wrong.
This is the inverse of stress and has the wrong units.

options.text: F divided by the length of the bar
options.rationale: Stress depends on area, not on the bar's length.

items.explanation: Correct: normal stress sigma = F/A for uniform axial loading.

items.stem: Fatigue failure in a machine component is primarily associated with:

options.rationale: Correct: fatigue arises from fluctuating stresses applied repeatedly.

options.text: A single static overload applied once
options.rationale: That is static failure, not fatigue.

options.text: Loads well below any stress whatsoever
options.rationale: Fatigue still requires fluctuating stress, not zero stress.

options.text: Only thermal expansion with no mechanical load
options.rationale: Fatigue is driven by cyclic mechanical stress, not expansion alone.

items.explanation: Correct: fatigue arises from fluctuating stresses applied repeatedly.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about static failure theories for ductile materials are generally correct?

options.text: The distortion-energy (von Mises) theory is commonly used for ductile materials
options.rationale: Correct: von Mises is a standard ductile-failure criterion.

options.text: The maximum-shear-stress theory is a conservative ductile criterion
options.rationale: Correct: Tresca (max-shear) is a common, more conservative ductile theory.

options.text: Ductile failure theories are based solely on the material's color
options.rationale: Color is irrelevant to failure theory.

options.text: Ductile materials never yield before fracture
options.rationale: Ductile materials characteristically yield before fracture.

options.text: Failure theories require no knowledge of the stress state
options.rationale: The stress state is essential input to any failure theory.

items.explanation: Correct keys: A, B. Correct: von Mises is a standard ductile-failure criterion. Correct: Tresca (max-shear) is a common, more conservative ductile theory.
